I replaced my thermistor as I learned that it should read about 11 k at room temp. Mine was reading a little higher. Both of the new ones read a little below 11 k but closer so I figured better to use these ones plus I figured a lower ohm reading would have the time thermistor shut the heat off earlier. The problem I was having is my thermal cutoff kept blowing so the heating element would not work. I don’t think the thermistor was my problem as the thermal cutoff continued to fail/blow.

Nonetheless, this thermistor seems to work well. I also have an extra as backup along with the one I removed. These should last the remaining life of my 20 year old dryer as thermistors do not seem to go bad very often.

Stay safe. Turn off the dryer breaker and unplug the dryer before conducting maintenance on it.

Easy to install and resolved the issue with my Whirlpool Duet gas dryer.  The part is very easy to install and I replaced both the thermistor and the thermal fuse.  20 minutes of work and $13 in parts and the gas ignited once I finished installing and tested the dryer.  Not much to the part but an inexpensive fix if your dryer is not heating up.

The two thermistors that i received did not operate within factory specifications.  the resistance at room temperature  was about right, but the resistance does not decrease at the proper rate as temperature rises.  This resulted in the drying temp to be about  30 degrees too hot on the "low temp" setting and  more than 40 degrees too hot on the "high temp"  I manually stopped the cycle when i saw exhaust temps exceed 200 degrees.  which is hot enough the blow the thermal fuse.  A factory spec'd thermistor shuts off the heat at about 160 degrees on "high" on my machine.

Part works. Installation is straight forward but there are tricky angles involved. Removing the screws required on my He3 from pre-2006 required a driver and some odd angles, but the biggest issue was the lint I found trapped inside the fan, fan housing and the filter plenum. It was SCARY!
Replacing the thermistor itself was a breeze once I got into it and I have attached a photo of the old one that caused the malfunction. I originally thought the plastic had worn away completely, revealing the semiconductor itself. But now I realize that the original OAM part looks quite different and the thermistor is supposed to be exposed. No idea if this will affect performance, but the new part looks very different from the old part.
I strongly recommend you take the time to clean all the tubes, housings, plenums and especially inside and around the burner housing so you don't end up with a dryer fire down the road.
